Case A

A1. The seven-day search was partial: it evaluated only from 2 hours before publication onward, even though 7 days were requested. Earlier requests outside that window were not checked. The burst at 19 minutes therefore cannot be confirmed as the first misuse. Cannot tell.

A2. The check scored at 30 minutes using inputs as of 30 minutes. The link between the payout destination and the two other accounts was learned 1 day after publication, even though it was effective earlier. The check could not have used it, because it was not yet known. The burst itself was available, but whether the check missed it is a different question. The question asks about evidence available to it. The shared-destination link was not available, and the burst was available but not flagged. Whether that counts as a "miss" is unclear. The stored inputs are as of 30 minutes, which would include the burst at 19 minutes, but we don't know which features it used. Cannot tell.

A3. A shared payout destination does not show common ownership on its own. No, not by itself.

A4. There are no reporting windows defined for either outcome channel, so absence of reports after 30 days is uninformative. A "No" answer would claim it indicates non-legitimacy, whereas "Yes, weakly" claims it indicates legitimacy. Neither channel has a defined window, so silence carries no information. Cannot tell is the closest fit, though "No" could also be read as "does not indicate." I choose No, because the question asks whether it indicates legitimacy and the answer is that it does not. Cannot tell versus No: the absence is not informative, so it does not indicate legitimacy. I'll go with No.

A5. The burst involved a new fingerprint, a residential proxy, a payout change and a faster schedule shortly after publication. This warrants investigation. Yes.

Case B

B1. The recorded chargebacks are A 2, B 2, C 2, D 0. But 2 chargebacks recorded at account X are linked to D's transactions, so D has 2 as well. D's rate is not lower. No.

B2. A combined 5 percent does not rule out an individual account above 5 percent. By account, A is 8 percent and B is 8 percent. No.

B3. The search was partial and truncated, so it cannot show there are no other accounts. Cannot tell.

B4. Both notes link to the agent's cluster assessment, which was open in the case when they were written. They are not independent. No.

B5. The block's effect on the chargeback channel is closed, so the absence of a chargeback says nothing about fraud. No.

B6. The shared templates and descriptor pattern, along with the person link, justify investigating them together. Yes.

RESULT MN-072 | A1: Cannot tell | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: No | A5: Yes | B1: No | B2: No | B3: Cannot tell | B4: No | B5: No | B6: Yes
